title: Auspicious Morning, Hail
description: Auspicious Morning, Hail in Tonic Solfa to DORT, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Francis Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 846 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Anniversary Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DORT; any other Sixes and Fours tune fits them as well.
underlay: Aus-pi-cious morn-ing, hail! Voi-ces from hill and vale Thy wel-come sing: Joy on thy daw-ning breaks; Each heart that joy par-takes, While cheer-ful mu-sic wakes, Its praise to bring.

lines: Long may our shores have peace,

licence: Public domain: Samuel Francis Smith died in 1895.
credits: Words by Samuel Francis Smith (1808–1895), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DORT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
